rules.text: Do not classify symmetric periventricular hyperintensities as anomalies if they appear bilaterally in the same anatomical region.
rules.justification: The agent falsely identified a symmetric, bilateral feature as a unilateral defect. This rule prevents flagging normal symmetric anatomical variations as anomalies.

rules.text: If ventricle morphology is symmetric and tissue texture is uniform, classify as normal even if subtle periventricular hyperintensities are present.
rules.justification: The agent overpredicted anomaly (0.5) on a normal case due to uncertainty about subtle periventricular features. This rule clarifies that such features are acceptable in normal scans when global symmetry and texture are preserved.

rules.text: Flag as anomaly if a large, heterogeneous mass with irregular borders and significant mass effect is present.
rules.justification: The agent underpredicted a clear case of a large, space-occupying lesion. This rule explicitly targets the visual features of such masses to ensure high-confidence detection.

rules.text: If a focal hyperintense lesion is detected in the posterior hemisphere, override refutation and classify as anomaly.
rules.justification: The agent initially detected the lesion but lowered the score due to refutation. This rule ensures that specific high-value features like posterior hyperintensities are not dismissed, correcting the underprediction.

rules.text: If initial visual inspection finds no candidate anomalous features, cap the final anomaly score at 0.25 to reflect high confidence in normality.
rules.justification: The agent correctly identified no anomalies but output a high uncertainty score (0.5). This rule forces a lower score when visual evidence strongly supports a normal classification, preventing false uncertainty.

rules.text: If a large hyperintense mass is detected in the cerebral hemisphere, immediately classify as anomaly regardless of initial uncertainty.
rules.justification: The agent initially detected the mass but lowered its score due to uncertainty. This rule forces a high anomaly score when such a distinct, large mass is present, preventing underprediction.

rules.text: If a large, irregular hyperintense mass with surrounding edema is detected, override any refutation and classify as anomaly.
rules.justification: The agent initially detected the mass and edema but incorrectly refuted them, leading to a low score. This rule ensures such distinct pathological features are prioritized over refutation logic.

rules.text: If a focal hyperintense lesion is detected in the periventricular region and absent in normal references, classify as anomaly.
rules.justification: The agent correctly identified the lesion but failed to commit to the anomaly class. This rule explicitly links the specific feature (periventricular hyperintensity) to the anomaly label, preventing uncertainty.

rules.text: Do not flag dark, fluid-filled ventricular structures in the brain's center as anomalies; these are normal anatomical features.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly identified the normal lateral ventricles as a defect. This rule explicitly defines this common anatomical structure as a normal variant to prevent false positives.

rules.text: Do not classify symmetric, bilateral ring-like hyperintensities in deep brain structures as anomalies; these are normal anatomical features.
rules.justification: The agent falsely identified symmetric deep brain structures as a unilateral lesion. This rule clarifies that such bilateral symmetry indicates normal anatomy, preventing false positives.
